catalog_quote: Itneg Inlaud is an Austronesian language spoken in Abra, Ilocos Norte, and Ilocos Sur in the northern Philippines. Facing rapid language loss and remaining largely undocumented, this study provides the first comprehensive grammatical description ... the study documents the sound system, core morphosyntax, and clause structures ... Its phonology is conservative, with 14 consonants, four vowels, phonemic stress, and common morphophonemic processes.

new_statements.rule_in_words: The author's abstract says only that stress is phonemic (contrastive), i.e. its position is not predictable from the segmental string; the abstract gives no position rule. The two SIL Inlaod/Binongan wordlists held by the project mark stress per word on either the penult or the final syllable, consistent with lexical stress, but they state no rule.
new_statements.domain_note: Abstract-level claim about the phonology of the language as a whole; no word/phrase domain discussion available. The full dissertation (ten chapters, includes the sound system) is unpublished and not online.
new_statements.identity_note: Target is Inlaod (Inlaud, western) Itneg, iti / inla1260. Himes 1997 (p. 103) treats Itneg as one language with two dialects, Binongan (eastern, itb / bino1237) and Inlaod (western). The only published phonemic sketch (Walton in Reid 1971) and Walton 1975 describe Binongan, not Inlaod; the SIL Binongan wordlist held held by the project is bino1237 material. Gonzales 2025 and the SIL Danglas wordlist are Inlaod proper (Danglas, Lagangilang, Peñarrubia, Langiden area).

sources.note: Sec. 2.2 'Itneg phonology' (p. 107) treats only segments (four-vowel system, /o/ for *u, diphthong reflexes); PKI inventory lists *V: (length) but nothing on stress placement in Itneg. Confirms Binongan and Inlaod as the two Itneg dialects (p. 103).
